results.title: Call of Duty game under fire for using real Itaewon crowd crush footage
results.content: The latest installment in the global Call of Duty game franchise drew condemnation from bereaved families and civic groups in South Korea after players discovered that it contained real footage from the 2022 Itaewon crowd crush. The game, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, depicts a full-scale North Korean invasion of South Korea, and initially drew attention in South Korea for its realistic portrayal of the country. However, the reception turned hostile after viewers identified what appeared to be real footage of bystanders performing CPR during the Itaewon tragedy during a sequence showing civilian casualties from the fictional war. The crowd crush killed more than 150 people on Oct. 29, 2022, and Thursday marks its fourth anniversary. results.title: Danpyunsun & The Moments Ensemble paints landscapes with music
results.content: Danpyunsun has long been a mainstay of Korea’s underground music scene, celebrated by critics and respected among those in the know. Then came 2024 and the formation of his new outfit, The Moments Ensemble. Their debut album, "Hail to the Music," was such a critical smash that the broader music scene could no longer ignore them. On Oct. 14, the band released its second album, "Lovers," which is both a sequel to the debut and a new direction. Here, the band explores its formation and the unique blend of sounds and approaches that has the scene so enamored. “I think the landscapes I paint through my music have changed significantly,” said Danpyunsun, describing how his work with The Moments Ensemble differs from his previous bands. A significant change shouldn’t come as a surprise, since Danpyunsun has been releasing music for over 20 years. He made his live debut in 2004 and became a much

results.title: Lotte Giants hire ex-manager as bench coach
results.content: The Lotte Giants on Wednesday brought back their former manager Her Mun-hoe as bench coach. The Giants said Her, 54, will also double as a hitting adviser, as the Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) club's offseason overhaul continued. On Monday, they named Lee Dong-wook, a former title-winning skipper for another KBO club, the NC Dinos, as their new manager. Lee Taek-keun, a former outfielder, was hired as the Giant's new general manager, despite having no prior experience either in coaching or in a front office role. Her managed the Giants in 2020 and in the early part of 2021. In his first season in charge, the Giants finished seventh among 10 KBO clubs at 71-72-1 (wins-losses-ties). The team fired him in May 2021, when they were stuck in last place at 12-18-0. Prior to his Giants managerial gig, Her had worked as the bench coach for the Kiwoom Heroes and as the hitting coach for both t

results.title: Korea fines Google, Apple combined $47.6 mil. over in-app payment practices
results.content: The Korean government on Wednesday slapped Google and Apple with a combined 63.7 billion won ($47.6 million) in fines for practices including forcing app developers to use their in-app payment systems, marking the first enforcement of the relevant provisions since Korea amended its law in 2021 to prohibit such practices. During a plenary session, the Korea Media and Communications Commission (KMCC) imposed fines of 42.9 billion won on Google and 20.81 billion won on Apple, along with corrective orders. The commission said the U.S. tech giants violated the Telecommunications Business Act, which prohibits app market operators from forcing developers to use specific payment methods. results.title: Finance minister hopes for Bloomberg review of Korea's market status
results.content: Korea's finance minister has said the country's classification as an emerging market in a Bloomberg bond index should be reviewed, citing its improved market access for foreign investors, the finance ministry said Wednesday. Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il made the remarks during a meeting with Bing Li, head of Asia-Pacific at Bloomberg L.P., to discuss ways to cooperate on the development of Korea's financial market. During the meeting, Lee said a review was needed to determine whether Korea's classification as an emerging market in the Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index remains appropriate. Lee noted that Korea is classified as a developed nation by the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, adding that Seoul has also made progress in improving market access for global investors. He called for Bloomberg's continued attention and cooperation to ensure these factors are reflected i

results.title: Appellate court reduces ex-PSS chief's sentence to 3 years
results.content: Park Jong-joon, former chief of the Presidential Security Service (PSS), was sentenced by an appellate court Wednesday to three years in prison for blocking investigators from executing a warrant to detain former President Yoon Suk Yeol last year. The sentence was reduced from the four years that a lower court handed down in July. Park and other former PSS officials were indicted for obstructing investigators' attempt to execute an arrest warrant for Yoon at the presidential residence in January 2025 over his imposition of martial law. The Seoul High Court said it reduced Park's sentence because he did not appear to have actively engaged in physical confrontations with officials seeking to execute the arrest warrant. It also said his resignation on Jan. 7 last year could be interpreted as an acknowledgment of responsibility for the resulting confusion and conflict. However, the high cour

results.title: Lotte opens sprawling anime, gaming hub at Busan department store
results.content: Lotte Department Store is set to open a sprawling retail space in Busan that brings anime, gaming, character merchandise and collectible figures together in one place. The department store’s Busan Main location will open Fandom Space on Friday on its basement first floor, spanning 1,785 square meters and carrying the slogan “Where Fandoms Come Alive.” The new zone brings together merchandise and experiences that have traditionally been scattered across specialty stores, aiming to give fans a place to shop, connect and celebrate their interests. The decision to launch the first location in Busan rather than Seoul reflects the growing appeal of the Seomyeon shopping district among younger consumers, particularly those in their 20s and 30s, according to the company. results.title: Seoul Design Week draws 670,000 visitors as city expands global reach
results.content: Seoul Design Week attracted 670,000 visitors over 12 days, turning the city into a sprawling showcase for design and consumer culture while drawing international attention ahead of Seoul’s hosting of the 2027 World Design Congress. Organized by the Seoul Metropolitan Government and the Seoul Design Foundation, the festival ran from Oct. 14 to 25, bringing together 871 companies and brands, 370 designers and 353 university students. This year’s edition expanded beyond Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) to 150 design destinations across five areas of Seoul, including Seongsu, Yeonhui, Seochon and Apgujeong, giving visitors opportunities to explore design in studios, exhibitions and everyday spaces. The DDP Design Fair, co-hosted with lifestyle commerce platform 29CM, drew 35,000 visitors over five days, with more than 80 brands presenting products under the theme “A market full of personal tast

results.title: Korean won sharply weakens against US dollar
results.content: The Korean won sharply weakened against the U.S. dollar Wednesday, as foreigners appeared to have purchased dollar futures and covered dollar-short positions. The won was quoted at 1,337.7 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., down 14 won from the close of the previous stock trading session. At one point in afternoon trading, the won dropped to a low of 1,342.3 won per dollar. Although the U.S. Federal Reserve is expected to leave its key policy rate unchanged this week, traders have been monitoring whether the U.S. central bank will hint at a rate hike later this year. Foreign investors purchased a net 815.8 billion won ($609 million) worth of local shares during the latest regular stock trading session, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index jumping 6.63 percent to close at 6,012.44.

results.title: Samsung Wallet Money goes global with app-free payments
results.content: Samsung Wallet Money, a prepaid payment service jointly operated by Samsung Electronics and Woori Bank, has expanded overseas, allowing users to pay with their Galaxy smartphones worldwide without installing local payment apps, Woori Bank said Wednesday. Unlike other mobile payment services that require users to install and open a separate app and complete additional authentication steps at checkout, Samsung Wallet Money lets them pay by tapping their Galaxy phone on a contactless terminal. Launched in Korea last year, the service has since surpassed 3 million users. Customers link a domestic bank account to their Wallet Money account to top up their balance and make payments. results.title: '44 minutes before rescuers reached her': Families view footage of foreign Itaewon victims' last moments
results.content: Families of foreign victims of the 2022 Itaewon crowd crush watched second-by-second footage of their loved ones’ final moments and said the recordings showed too few police officers at the scene and a rescue response that came too late. “Yesterday was a difficult day for me. I watched my sister’s final moments, where she walked and how she died,” Damira Sherniyazova, who traveled from Kazakhstan, said during a press conference in Seoul Wednesday. Her sister, Madina, was among the 26 foreign nationals killed in the crowd crush that claimed 159 lives in a narrow Seoul alley four years ago. A total of 35 members of 18 families across 10 countries arrived in Korea at the government’s invitation starting Friday to mark the fourth anniversary of the tragedy. results.title: Korean-US security talks unlikely to take place this year amid scheduling difficulties
results.content: The annual defense chiefs’ meeting between Korea and the United States appears increasingly unlikely to take place this year, as Washington expects it to be pushed back to early 2027 while Seoul maintains that no final decision has been made. The uncertainty over the Security Consultative Meeting (SCM) comes as Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul met his U.S. counterpart Pete Hegseth for the first time Wednesday on the sidelines of a regional defense meeting in the Philippine province of Cebu. Before departing for the Philippines, Kang said the SCM schedule might need to be discussed with Washington, noting that the U.S. side had its own circumstances to consider. “There are circumstances on their side, so I think we need to hear what they have to say,” Kang told reporters when asked whether the meeting could be pushed beyond December. results.title: Korea accepts int'l arbitration in favor of Elliott in Samsung merger case
results.content: Korea will accept an international arbitration ruling in favor of U.S. hedge fund Elliott Investment Management over the 2015 merger of two Samsung affiliates, the justice ministry said Wednesday. The ministry decided not to file a suit seeking a cancellation of last month's ruling, which ordered Korea to pay about 153 billion won ($114 million) in damages plus interest to Elliott. Elliott originally filed the case in 2018, seeking compensation over losses from the controversial merger between Samsung C&T and Cheil Industries. The U.S. hedge fund, which was a minority stakeholder of Samsung C&T, argued unfair mediation by the Korean government in the merger's approval. An international tribunal ruled in favor of Elliott in 2023, but the Korean government took the case to the High Court in London. results.title: DPK launches advisory body on foreign affairs, inter-Korean ties
results.content: The ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) on Wednesday launched an advisory council on foreign affairs, security and unification to review policies and support the Lee Jae Myung administration's "pragmatic" diplomacy. At the council's inaugural meeting, DPK leader Kim Min-seok stressed the importance of expanding cooperation with neighboring countries while maintaining a strong Korea-U.S. alliance. "The key to a pragmatic foreign policy centered on national interests lies in maintaining the unwavering Korea-U.S. alliance and strengthening our diplomatic and security foundations based on that alliance, while expanding cooperation with neighboring countries like China and Japan," he said. Kim vowed to ensure that the council's recommendations are reflected in the party's foreign and security policies, as well as those of the government. DPK Rep. results.title: Unification minister urges N. Korea to join talks on inter-Korean border
results.content: Unification Minister Chung Dong-young on Wednesday urged North Korea to accept the South's proposal last week for military talks on the inter-Korean border. Seoul proposed the talks Friday, after a land mine blast inside the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) on Sept. 21 wounded three South Korean soldiers, two of them seriously. The South wants to jointly verify where the land-based Military Demarcation Line (MDL) separating the two Koreas sits, restore military communication lines and discuss ways to prevent accidental clashes. "South and North Korea should align their positions on the MDL through dialogue, and establish a communication system for peaceful management of the area as soon as possible," he said in an address read by a senior ministry official at the DMZ Open Eco Peace Forum in Goyang, just northwest of Seoul. results.title: 1VERSE releases debut mini album, expands world tour in 2027
results.content: K-pop boy group 1VERSE will release its first mini album and embark on its second world tour in 2027, opening a new chapter for the group as it seeks to reach audiences across more continents. Korean music label Singing Beetle announced the plans, Wednesday, saying the projects would mark the end of the group’s “SHATTERED” era. The mini album will feature songs self-produced by the members, according to the label, which did not disclose the release date, album title or track list. The upcoming tour will expand beyond North America and Europe, where the group performed during its first world tour, although the label has not yet identified the additional regions it plans to visit. The group’s next chapter has been made possible in part by a crowdfunding project powered by 5TARZ, its fandom, with support from fans around the world, the announcement said. results.title: Seoul Forest pop-up draws 43,000 visitors, with foreigners making up one-quarter
results.content: Nearly one in four visitors to a Seoul-branded pop-up store at Seoul Forest were foreign tourists, driving total attendance past 42,000 over three months as municipal authorities work to capitalize on the city's global profile through official merchandise. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Wednesday that 42,738 people visited The Seoul My Soul Lounge from July 31 to Tuesday during the 2026 Seoul International Garden Show. Foreign visitors numbered 10,272, accounting for 24 percent of the total, according to the city. Set up on a lawn at Seoul Forest, the lounge combined garden displays with merchandise and food products designed to showcase Seoul’s identity, expanding on the city’s existing Seoul My Soul promotional spaces. results.title: Lee's 'migrant workers don't contribute much' remarks fall short of embracing Korea's growing diversity
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung said Tuesday that migrant workers “don’t contribute much to the national economy” because they send their earnings home. When criticism followed his remarks at a Cabinet meeting, he focused on a word missing from a newspaper headline — “much.” But restoring that word does little to address the larger question of whether the president sees foreign workers as members of Korea's increasingly diverse society or mainly judges their worth by where they spend their wages. Lee made the remarks while instructing officials to consider wage subsidies to attract Korean workers to agriculture. “For national security reasons, we must sustain agriculture, forestry, livestock farming and fisheries,” he said. “Bringing in foreign workers doesn’t contribute much to the national economy because they send all their earnings home.” After The Hankyoreh, a local daily newspaper, reporte

results.title: Made in Korea content is here to stay
results.content: If you look closely at the credits of some of the most popular and widely distributed content worldwide, it would be rare to find that Koreans had not been materially involved in the creative and production process. What has changed is that the Kims, Parks and the like are increasingly appearing at the forefront of the value chain and workflow — not simply contributing behind the scenes, but shaping and leading the creative process itself. I first noticed this years ago while watching "The Simpsons." I remember thinking, somewhat proudly, that we Koreans were doing some really great, cool stuff — and, more importantly, stuff of global relevance. results.title: Foreign resident population in Korea hits record 2.66 mil. as int'l student numbers surge
results.content: The number of foreign residents living in Korea rose for the fourth consecutive year in 2025 to reach a record high of 2.66 million, driven largely by a sharp increase in international students, government data showed Wednesday. According to the 2025 Foreign Resident Status report released by the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, foreign residents totaled 2,662,967 as of Nov. 1 last year. The figure represents a 3.1 percent increase, or 79,341 people, from 2,583,626 a year earlier, based on census data compiled by the National Data Agency. Foreign residents now account for 5.1 percent of Korea’s total population of 51,817,499 — the highest proportion on record. The ministry defines foreign residents as individuals residing in the country for more than 90 days who hold foreign nationality, have acquired Korean citizenship or were born in Korea to foreign-national or naturalized parents

results.title: Defense chiefs of S. Korea, US hold talks on OPCON transfer, alliance
results.content: The defense chiefs of South Korea and the United States met in the Philippines on Wednesday for talks likely centered on narrowing differences over the timing of the wartime operational control (OPCON) transition from Washington to Seoul, among other alliance issues. The talks between Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul and U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth took place in Cebu, the venue for the ASEAN Defense Ministers' Meeting (ADMM) Plus, led by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), according to Seoul's defense ministry. It marked their first one-on-one meeting since Kang took office in September. Further details of their meeting were expected to be released later in the day. Wednesday's talks have drawn attention as Seoul seeks to regain wartime OPCON before the Lee Jae Myung administration's five-year term ends in 2030. results.title: US Silver Star Medal reissued to late S. Korean veteran of Korean War
results.content: A late South Korean veteran who was awarded the U.S. Silver Star Medal for his role in a Korean War battle in 1952 has recently been reissued the medal posthumously after it went missing decades ago, officials said Wednesday. Late Army Staff Sgt. Nam Woon-soo was given the U.S. honor, as well as the Chungmu Order of Military Merit from the South Korean government, in 1953 for playing a key role in the Battle of White Horse Hill in what is the current border town of Cheorwon, some 80 kilometers northeast of Seoul. During the battle, Nam crawled his way up to the entrance of the enemy's position and destroyed it, making a decisive contribution to neutralizing enemy firepower. It was one of the Korean War's most fiercely fought battles between the U.S.-backed South Korean forces and the communist troops from China. results.title: Lula's surprise win hits Korean investors in Brazil bonds
results.content: Korean investors who piled into high-yield Brazilian bonds ahead of the country's presidential election are nursing losses after Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's surprise victory sent bond yields soaring and the currency tumbling, analysts said Wednesday. Brazilian government bonds have been popular among wealthy Korean investors, offering annual yields of around 10 percent and tax-free interest income under a bilateral tax treaty between Korea and Brazil. Korean investors purchased a net $5.53 million worth of Brazilian bonds in September, nearly four times the $1.39 million recorded the previous month, according to SEIBro, a data portal operated by the Korea Securities Depository. They continued to buy Brazilian bonds this month, with net purchases totaling $1.78 million through Tuesday. results.title: Global trekkers climb Seoul's rocky mountain trails for scenic views, nature
results.content: Under a clear autumn sky, 18 international hikers from diverse backgrounds gathered outside Exit 1 of Gwanaksan Station on Monday to kick off the three-week "2026 Seoul Hiking Week: Autumn." Their objective for Day 1 was Mount Hoam, one of the peaks on the larger Mount Gwanak in southern Seoul, an "extreme course" route designed to showcase Seoul's rugged urban terrain. Running through Nov. 15, the Seoul Hiking Week is centered around three mountains in Seoul: Mount Bukhan, Mount Bugak and Mount Gwanak. Before hitting the trail, participants stopped at the Seoul Hiking Tourism Center directly connected to the station. By scanning a simple QR code, trekkers accessed a complimentary equipment rental service that provided everything from hiking poles, gloves and backpacks to windbreakers and hiking boots. results.title: HD Hyundai Q3 net profit up 40% to $1 bil.
results.content: HD Hyundai, the holding company of Korea's leading shipbuilding conglomerate, said Wednesday its third-quarter net profit jumped 40 percent from a year earlier, driven by strong performances across its shipbuilding, machinery and energy businesses. Net profit for the July-September period came to 1.38 trillion won ($1 bil.), up from 986.9 billion won a year earlier, the company said in a regulatory filing based on consolidated earnings. Operating profit for the July-September period surged 71.5 percent on-year to 2.91 trillion won, while revenue rose 21.2 percent to 22.08 trillion won. In the shipbuilding and marine engineering sector, HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering, the group's shipbuilding subholding company, reported a 9.3 percent increase in sales to 8.28 trillion won and a 37.3 percent rise in operating profit to 1.44 trillion won, supported by robust demand for high-v

results.title: Korea eyes 30 mil. tourists with regional push
results.content: Korea is working to open an era of 30 million foreign visitors by shifting its tourism focus from Seoul to regional areas, Culture Minister Chae Hwi-young said Wednesday. "An unprecedented future has already arrived and Korea is fully preparing to welcome 30 million and eventually 40 million overseas travelers," Chae said during a press conference in Seoul. "To ensure that regional tourism genuinely drives local economies, we will manage not just the total number of inbound visitors, but also focus on qualitative growth while actively addressing overtourism concerns." The country's tourism sector is currently riding a wave of record-breaking growth, with cumulative foreign tourist arrivals surpassing the 2025 annual total of 18.94 million as of Tuesday. results.title: Sangmidang seeks North American, European expansion through global partnerships
results.content: Hur Jin-soo, vice chairman of Korean bakery giant Sangmidang Holdings, met Gellert Global Group (GGG) Chairman George Gellert and U.S. Ambassador to France Charles Kushner in Paris earlier this week to explore broader partnerships in overseas markets. Sangmidang said Wednesday that Hur discussed business developments and potential cooperation with Gellert and other GGG executives. Samlip, Sangmidang’s mass-market bakery subsidiary, could work with GGG to expand through U.S. supermarket and food service distribution networks and potentially enter Canada and Mexico, the Korean company said. U.S.-based GGG imports and distributes food products to retailers, food service distributors, restaurants, hotels, cruise operators and food manufacturers across North America. results.title: Hanwha's KAI bid bodes well for another defense leap forward
results.content: Hanwha Group’s potential acquisition of Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) could give the country’s aerospace and defense industry a much-needed boost in the global market, as privately owned defense firms have significantly outpaced their state-backed rival in sales growth. Yet transferring control of a strategically important company to a private conglomerate would also raise questions over national security, market concentration and the public investment underpinning its technological achievements. KAI has remained under state ownership since its establishment in 1999, with the state-run Export-Import Bank of Korea as its largest shareholder, holding a 26.41 percent stake. Hanwha is the second-largest shareholder, with a 15.89 percent stake. results.title: Debate grows over KAI privatization as Hanwha aims to expand stake
results.content: The privatization of Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) could gain momentum as the state-run Export-Import Bank of Korea (Eximbank) commissions a 1.8 billion won ($1.36 million) consulting project and the Fair Trade Commission (FTC) highlights the benefits of stronger competition among major defense companies. Although Eximbank and KAI have expressed reservations about a change in ownership, KAI’s slower growth compared to its defense industry peers, despite a boom in arms exports, is fueling calls for privatization. Eximbank is KAI’s largest shareholder, with a 26.41 percent stake. According to Rep. Ahn Sang-hoon of the main opposition People Power Party and other sources, Eximbank recently selected AT Kearney as the preferred bidder for the consulting project and is proceeding with the subsequent steps. results.title: EMAT seeks to reduce reliance on Chinese rare earth magnets with Pohang facility
results.content: Evolution Metals & Technologies (EMAT), a Nasdaq-listed rare earth magnet producer, is making a big bet on Pohang, North Gyeongsang Province, by building a facility capable of producing 10,000 tons of sintered rare earth magnets annually for export to the U.S. and to other global customers seeking to reduce their reliance on China's dominant rare earth supply chain. The company plans to invest approximately 300 billion won ($224 million) in Pohang, including 223.8 billion won earmarked for building initial production capacity on a 118,000-square-meter site at the Blue Valley Industrial Complex in the city by 2027. EMAT and the Pohang city government signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) on the investment project on Tuesday, with the city pledging administrative support for EMAT's plans.
